heading: Rust, Go and C# on the web
body: A service written only in Rust, only in Go or only in C# needs no browser sibling on the web. Rust links on the three desktops, C# links on Windows, and Go links on no host. Where a host links the service, it runs natively. Everywhere else, including the web, it runs as WebAssembly: in the browser, or in the web view of a native target (ADR 0035, ADR 0037, ADR 0045; an ADR is an architecture decision record). Rust compiles with rustc --target wasm32-unknown-unknown into one small module. Go compiles into one module for all the Go services of the application. A release build compiles it with TinyGo, which leaves out most of the Go runtime, so a small service is about 360 KB (115 KB as sent with Brotli). Without TinyGo, or when TinyGo cannot compile the services, the standard Go compiler (GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm) builds a module that carries the whole Go runtime and starts at about 2.7 MB. The page loads the module with the wasm_exec.js of the compiler that built it (see WebAssembly compilers per language, ADR 0081). C# publishes onto the .NET browser runtime. That runtime is about 3 MB, and the service worker caches it once. F# services compile into a small F# library that runs on the same .NET browser runtime, so a page with C# and F# services loads that runtime once; no host links F#, so an F# service runs as WebAssembly on every target, Windows included (ADR 0073). So when a service has several of these versions, Tachyon uses Rust, then Go, then C#, then F# (Choose a service language gives the full order). The page speaks the same companion protocol as a native host, so the service is the same file. Its fields render, and so does a model from client/models, a list of models and a model inside a model. Its methods take JSON arguments. In Rust, these are String, &str, bool, numbers, TacValue, models, and Vec or Option of them. In Go, they are string, bool, numbers, slices, maps or structs. In C# and F#, they are string, bool, numbers, object, models and lists of models. The page reaches only these members. A Rust field or method of another type, such as the HTTPClient a service holds, stays inside the service. A C# member reaches the page only when it is public or internal. A Rust model derives Clone, because the page reads a copy of the field. A model field named with a Rust keyword uses a raw identifier, such as `pub r#type: String`; the page and the JSON see it as `type`. An F# service shows its `member val` properties and its public members. A view reaches the exported Go members with a lower-case first letter, so Count is {tally.count}. Service and NeedsAll sit on their own lines above the type. Rust spells Service as #[Service], Go spells it as // @Service, C# spells it as [Service], and F# spells it as [<Service>]. A bare constructor lets every field take the property with the same name, and it makes the service one per component. In F#, [<NeedsAll>] marks the primary constructor, so its parameters take the properties. A WebAssembly service has no DOM and no platform. It is state and logic over the properties its tag passes. It also runs on the page thread, like the page's own JavaScript (ADR 0084). A long computation in a method blocks clicks and keys until it ends, and the .NET runtime blocks the page while it starts. Move heavy work to the server. Those properties may carry a data file: the start-up request may carry up to 1 MiB (1048576 bytes) in Rust, Go, C#, F#, Swift, Kotlin, Java, Ruby, Lua and Python. Every later request, such as a method call, may carry up to 64 KiB (65536 bytes). A bigger request fails, and the error names the service, the size and the limit, for example: Web service documentation: The request is 1072202 bytes. The limit is 1048576 bytes. Pass less data to the service. A method call names the method too: The request to add is 70121 bytes. ty doctor checks for the wasm32-unknown-unknown target, Go 1.27 and the .NET wasm-tools workload. It also lists TinyGo and Binaryen's wasm-opt as optional tools: release builds use them to make the modules smaller.
